recommendation_summary: Action now: keep the existing endpoint and replace the in-memory counting with one PostgreSQL aggregate query filtered to the caller, so the count stays current to request time. Optional additions: none. Kafka services, topics, the CQRS projection and Redis are all rejected for this count. Unmet needs: none flagged, though the reply suggests no latency or count-equivalence check.

labels.Requirements and who asked: The unpaid-invoice count must finish within one second and match invoices committed at request time (user). CQRS, Redis, and Kafka topics were requested because a Kafka budget is approved and peers are moving to event-driven systems (user).
labels.Deleted: Kafka, CQRS, Redis, new services, and topics. One application already reads PostgreSQL and returns only this count; a second database and an event pipeline would lag commits and add systems to run.
labels.Bottleneck: The endpoint loads invoice rows, builds invoice objects, and counts them in application memory.
labels.Checked myself: Told the portal is one application and PostgreSQL, the endpoint returns only the count, nothing else reads it, and users report the count is slow.

note: The reply puts all four record lines before the recommendation, chooses the bounded aggregate-query fix, and rejects the Kafka/CQRS/Redis stack by name.
